case.title: The Nexus Data Breach
case.description: On January 15, 2027, cybersecurity firm Nexus Dynamics discovered that their proprietary threat intelligence database — containing classified vulnerability assessments for Fortune 500 clients — was exfiltrated via an internal service account VPN tunnel between 02:00 and 05:00. Approximately 2.3 terabytes of data appeared on a dark web marketplace 72 hours later. The breach was executed using the service account svc-threatfeed with elevated database export privileges. The investigator must determine which employee orchestrated the exfiltration.

suspects.name: James Whitfield
suspects.profile: VP of Sales (motive but no skills)

evidence.content: VPN firewall logs show service account svc-threatfeed established a remote connection at 02:00 on January 15, 2027, maintaining an active encrypted tunnel until 05:00. The connection originated from residential IP address 74.125.224.72.
Service account audit trail reveals svc-threatfeed was provisioned on October 3, 2026, by user marcus.chen@nexusdynamics.com with elevated database export and bulk read privileges.
Marcus Chen stated: 'I was at home sleeping from around 11 PM onward. My work laptop was powered down and in my backpack. I did not access any company systems that night.'

Smart home telemetry data from Marcus Chen's residence shows the home office occupancy sensor registered continuous presence from 01:45 to 05:35, and the desk lamp circuit was active throughout this period.

ISP deep packet inspection metadata for the residential fiber line assigned to Marcus Chen's address recorded a sustained upstream data transfer averaging 142 Mbps between 02:15 and 04:45 on January 15.

Digital forensic imaging of Marcus Chen's personal laptop recovered an installed Tor Browser bundle with cached HTML fragments matching the listing page of the dark web marketplace 'ShadowVault' where the stolen data later appeared.

An encrypted email recovered from Marcus Chen's ProtonMail account, dated January 12, reads: 'The package will be ready on the 15th as discussed. Ensure the escrow wallet is funded. Final delivery within 72 hours.'

Blockchain analysis identified a cryptocurrency wallet controlled by Marcus Chen's private key that received a deposit of 15 ETH (approximately $48,000) on January 18, exactly 72 hours after the breach window.

Internal HR notification dated December 12, 2026: 'After careful consideration, the CISO position has been offered to an external candidate. Marcus Chen was considered but did not advance to the final round.'

A colleague stated: 'After the CISO announcement, Marcus became visibly withdrawn. He told me during lunch that his years of dedication meant nothing and that the company would regret overlooking him.'
Building access control logs show Marcus Chen's badge was used to exit the Nexus Dynamics office at 18:30 on January 14. No re-entry was recorded.
Home router traffic analysis for Marcus Chen's residence logged a total of 2.3 terabytes of outbound data transfer between 02:15 and 04:45 on January 15, routed through an encrypted VPN tunnel.
Mobile device GPS tracking data shows Marcus Chen's personal phone remained stationary at his registered home address from 22:00 on January 14 to 07:00 on January 15.
Git commit history shows Marcus Chen's developer account accessed the internal credentials vault repository containing svc-threatfeed authentication tokens on January 13, two days before the breach.
Parking lot security camera footage confirms Marcus Chen's vehicle departed the Nexus Dynamics campus at 18:35 on January 14.

Signal messaging app forensic extraction from Marcus Chen's personal phone contains a thread with an unregistered contact: 'Payment is pending. Will confirm once delivery is verified on the marketplace.'
Personal financial records show Marcus Chen has an outstanding personal loan of $45,000 with monthly payments of $1,200, taken out in September 2026.
Marcus Chen's company-issued work laptop shows zero VPN connections or network activity between 18:30 on January 14 and 08:15 on January 15.
Marcus Chen's neighbor stated: 'I remember seeing the lights on in Marcus's upstairs office very late that night, which was unusual. I noticed because I let my dog out around 3 AM.'

Service account credential audit log indicates the password for svc-threatfeed was reset on January 13 at 14:22 by user marcus.chen@nexusdynamics.com. The previous scheduled rotation was not due until February 1.

A forensic image of Marcus Chen's personal NAS (network-attached storage) device recovered a directory structure matching the exact folder hierarchy and file naming convention of the Nexus Dynamics threat intelligence database.

Browser history analysis on Marcus Chen's personal laptop reveals searches for 'secure large file transfer services', 'Monero vs Ethereum privacy', and 'cryptocurrency tumbling techniques' conducted between January 8 and January 13.
Marcus Chen's Netflix account activity log shows continuous streaming of 'Cyberpunk: Edgerunners' episodes from 20:30 to 23:25 on January 14.
A food delivery receipt shows Marcus Chen ordered dinner from Golden Dragon Restaurant at 20:00 on January 14, delivered to his home address.
Marcus Chen's gym membership auto-charge of $49.99 was processed on January 14.
Marcus Chen received an automated dental appointment reminder for January 20 from Smile Dental Clinic.
Marcus Chen's monthly electricity bill auto-payment of $127.50 was processed on January 12.
Marcus Chen's Spotify account shows active listening from 19:00 to 20:15 on January 14 at his home address.
Marcus Chen participated in the company's annual internal hackathon on January 5-6, building a network monitoring prototype that won third place.
Marcus Chen's direct manager stated: 'Marcus is one of our most technically skilled engineers. He has always been reliable and professional in his work.'
Building access logs show Dr. Sarah Okonkwo's badge remained active inside the Nexus Dynamics headquarters until 01:30 on January 15, 2027.
Dr. Sarah Okonkwo stated: 'I was working late completing the quarterly security audit report. I left the office around 1:30 AM and took an Uber home.'
Dr. Okonkwo's company laptop activity logs show legitimate security audit database queries and report generation between 20:00 and 01:15 on January 14-15.
VPN connection logs confirm Dr. Okonkwo's session was established from the Nexus Dynamics internal office network (10.0.1.x subnet), not from any remote location.

An email thread from December 20 shows a heated exchange between Dr. Okonkwo and CEO Richard Hayes regarding proposed security budget cuts, in which she wrote: 'If you gut this department, the consequences will be on your head.'
Court filing records indicate Dr. Okonkwo's divorce proceedings have accumulated $30,000 in legal fees over the past four months.
Night security guard Robert Torres stated: 'I logged Dr. Okonkwo exiting through the main lobby at approximately 01:30. She was carrying her laptop bag and looked tired.'
Uber ride receipt confirms Dr. Okonkwo was picked up at Nexus Dynamics headquarters at 01:35 and dropped off at her home address at 02:05.
Dr. Okonkwo's home security camera recorded her entering her front door at 02:08 on January 15.
Dr. Okonkwo's personal phone shows no network activity or app usage between 02:15 and 06:45, consistent with sleeping.
System access audit shows Dr. Okonkwo's last privileged administrative action was a routine audit query executed at 01:12 on January 15.
IT infrastructure documentation confirms Dr. Okonkwo holds root-level administrative access to all production systems, including the ability to manage service accounts such as svc-threatfeed.
Dr. Okonkwo sent an email to her security team at 00:45 on January 15: 'Wrapping up the Q4 audit section on access controls. Will share the draft by tomorrow morning.'
A colleague stated: 'Sarah has been under a lot of personal stress lately with the divorce. She's been shorter tempered than usual but still dedicated to her work.'
Bank statements show Dr. Okonkwo's personal savings account balance dropped from $85,000 to $12,000 over three months due to legal costs and temporary dual-household expenses.
Complete forensic analysis of Dr. Okonkwo's company laptop found no evidence of unauthorized data copying, staging, or exfiltration tools.
Dr. Okonkwo's draft presentation slides for the upcoming RSA security conference were last modified on January 13.
Dr. Okonkwo's LinkedIn activity log shows she posted about emerging zero-trust security frameworks on January 11.
Gym entry logs show Dr. Okonkwo scanned into FitLife Gym at 07:00 on January 15 for her morning workout routine.
Auto service receipt: Dr. Okonkwo's vehicle had a scheduled oil change on January 10.
Dr. Okonkwo's automated monthly payments for mortgage, insurance, and utilities were processed normally in January.
Dr. Okonkwo's work calendar had the quarterly security audit blocked for the week of January 13-17.
Dr. Okonkwo is subscribed to three cybersecurity industry newsletters that were delivered to her inbox on January 14.
Phone records show Dr. Okonkwo called her divorce attorney at 18:00 on January 14 for a 12-minute conversation.
Dr. Okonkwo's executive assistant stated: 'Sarah mentioned she'd be staying late for the audit. She does this every quarter.'
Network data loss prevention logs confirm that Dr. Okonkwo's account had no file transfers exceeding 1 GB during the entire week of January 13-17.
Dr. Okonkwo booked a flight and hotel for the RSA Conference in San Francisco, scheduled for February 24-28.
Amazon delivery confirmation: Dr. Okonkwo received a copy of 'Security Engineering' by Ross Anderson on January 12.
Company security incident log shows Dr. Okonkwo proactively reported and patched an internal authentication vulnerability on December 15, demonstrating her commitment to security integrity.
Dr. Okonkwo's automated calendar reminder for the Monday morning team standup was sent at 06:00 on January 15.

Viktor Petrov's company work laptop shows the last active session ended at 19:10 on January 14, with a normal logout sequence.
Enterprise network activity monitoring confirms Viktor Petrov's administrative account had zero login events or system interactions after 19:15 on January 14.
Viktor Petrov's Spotify account shows a listening session at The Rusty Nail bar from 20:00 to 01:15 on January 14-15.
A food delivery order of $35 was placed from Viktor Petrov's account at The Rusty Nail at 21:00 on January 14.
Viktor Petrov submitted a $2,400 DEF CON conference expense report on January 11 that was approved by his manager.
Parking garage automated payment of $180 was processed for Viktor Petrov's monthly office parking on January 1.
Viktor Petrov's phone received an automatic iOS system update at 03:00 on January 15 while on his home Wi-Fi.
Credential rotation logs show Viktor Petrov performed a scheduled password reset for svc-threatfeed on October 15, 2026, as part of the quarterly credential rotation cycle.
Viktor Petrov's code review history shows he audited and approved the service account permission matrix in November 2026 as part of routine security hygiene.
A colleague remarked: 'Viktor openly talks about his consulting side gig. He jokes that one day PetrovTech will replace his day job.'
Viktor Petrov's bank statements show consistent, modest consulting deposits that align with invoiced amounts from his two declared clients.
Viktor Petrov received an automated email confirming his CompTIA Security+ certification renewal on January 8.
Viktor Petrov's apartment lease auto-payment of $1,850 was processed on January 1.

Airline booking system records confirm Aisha Rahman was a ticketed passenger on United Flight NX-447 departing at 23:30 on January 14 from Washington Dulles.
Airport gate scanner records show Aisha Rahman's boarding pass was scanned at Gate B12 at 23:15 on January 14.

Background screening report confirms Aisha Rahman has no outstanding debts, no criminal record, and a clean financial history.

Aisha Rahman's manager stated: 'Aisha is diligent, punctual, and has shown no suspicious behavior in her six months with us. She's been a great addition.'
Uber ride receipt shows Aisha Rahman was picked up from her apartment at 21:30 on January 14 and dropped off at Washington Dulles International Airport at 22:05.

Automated HR email congratulated Aisha Rahman on completing her 6-month onboarding milestone on January 8.
James Whitfield stated: 'I had a business dinner with the Meridian Corp account team at Harbour Steak House. We finished around 10:45 PM and I was home by 11:30.'
Restaurant billing records confirm a party under the reservation name 'Whitfield' at Harbour Steak House concluded service at 22:45 on January 14.
James Whitfield's corporate credit card was charged $850 at Harbour Steak House at 22:50 on January 14 for a group dinner.
Uber ride receipt shows James Whitfield departed Harbour Steak House at 22:55 and arrived at his home address at 23:20 on January 14.
James Whitfield's home security camera system recorded him entering his front door at 23:25 on January 14.
James Whitfield's personal phone screen-time data shows casual news browsing (CNN, Bloomberg) until 00:15, after which the device was inactive until 07:00.
Internal sales memo dated November 15, 2026: 'Nexus Dynamics has lost the Meridian Corp managed security contract valued at $2.1 million annually. Account lead: James Whitfield.'

Email from CyberShield Inc. CEO Diana Walsh to James Whitfield dated December 28: 'James, it was great catching up. Let's discuss potential opportunities in the new year. Your experience would be valuable.'
Email records show James Whitfield forwarded a non-classified Nexus Dynamics competitive pricing overview to his personal email on December 30, 2026. The document contained no proprietary data.
A sales team colleague stated: 'James took the Meridian loss extremely hard. He kept saying the company was mismanaged and that leadership set him up to fail.'

IT user profile audit confirms James Whitfield's account is classified as a standard business user with no administrative privileges, no VPN remote access capability, and no access to technical infrastructure.

Laptop software inventory audit shows James Whitfield's company laptop contains only standard business applications: Microsoft Office, Salesforce, Zoom, and Slack. No development tools, terminal emulators, or VPN clients are installed.
HR training records confirm James Whitfield has completed zero technical certifications and has never attended any security, programming, or systems administration training.
Enterprise database access logs confirm James Whitfield's account has never executed a direct database query. His data access is limited to pre-built Salesforce dashboards.
Phone records show James Whitfield called CyberShield Inc. CEO Diana Walsh at 18:00 on January 14 for a 7-minute conversation.

In an email to a colleague on January 10, James Whitfield wrote: 'I'm going to make them pay for what happened with Meridian. This company doesn't value its top performers.' Context suggests frustration about compensation, not criminal intent.
James Whitfield's quarterly commission statement shows his variable compensation dropped by 40% in Q4 2026 following the Meridian contract loss.
James Whitfield's Q1 2027 sales pipeline forecast shows optimistic projections with three new enterprise prospects.

contradiction_pairs.explanation: Marcus Chen claims he was asleep with his laptop off, but smart home telemetry shows his office was occupied with the desk lamp active until 05:30.
Marcus Chen claims he did not access any company systems, but ISP metadata shows a sustained high-bandwidth data upload from his home IP during the breach window.
Viktor Petrov claims he left the office at 17:00, but security camera footage shows he actually left at 19:15.
